Saving and loading models

Source: vignettes/model-files.Rmd
model-files.Rmd
library(simcompR)

Models can be written to declarative JSON files and read back. A file describes block types, names, parameters, connections, events and nested subsystems. It never contains R code that is executed when the file is read.

Round trip 

m <- sim_model("feedback", params = list(k = 2))
sim_add_block(m, "step", "r", time = 1)
sim_add_block(m, "subtract", "e")
sim_add_block(m, "gain", "g", gain = sim_param("k"))
sim_add_block(m, "transfer_function", "plant", num = 1, den = c(1, 0.3))
sim_connect(m, "r", "e", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "plant", "e", input = 2)
sim_connect(m, "e", "g")
sim_connect(m, "g", "plant")

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
sim_write_json(m, f)
m2 <- sim_read_json(f)

r1 <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), c(0, 5))
r2 <- sim_run(sim_compile(m2), c(0, 5))
identical(r1$signals, r2$signals)
#> [1] TRUE

The results are bit-for-bit identical because every number is stored in a form that reads back to the same double: a short decimal such as "0.1" where that is exact, and the hexadecimal form of C99 ("0x1.5555555555555p-2" for 1/3) otherwise. Matrices keep their dimensions and storage type.

The format 

cat(head(readLines(f), 40), sep = "\n")
#> {
#>   "schema": "simcompR.model",
#>   "schema_version": 1,
#>   "name": "feedback",
#>   "params": {
#>     "k": {
#>       "$num": [
#>         "2"
#>       ]
#>     }
#>   },
#>   "blocks": [
#>     {
#>       "name": "r",
#>       "type": "step",
#>       "params": {
#>         "time": {
#>           "$num": [
#>             "1"
#>           ]
#>         }
#>       }
#>     },
#>     {
#>       "name": "e",
#>       "type": "subtract",
#>       "params": {}
#>     },
#>     {
#>       "name": "g",
#>       "type": "gain",
#>       "params": {
#>         "gain": {
#>           "$param": "k"
#>         }
#>       }
#>     },
#>     {
#>       "name": "plant",
#>       "type": "transfer_function",

The top-level fields are schema ("simcompR.model"), schema_version (currently 1), name, params, blocks, connections and events. Encoded values:

JSON form R value
{"$num": ["0.10000000000000001"]} numeric vector, exact
{"$matrix": {"nrow": 2, "ncol": 2, "data": [...]}} numeric matrix
{"$int": ["1", "NA"]} integer vector
{"$chr": ["a", null]}, {"$lgl": [...]}, {"$list": [...]} other vectors and lists; null is a missing string
{"$param": "k"} sim_param("k")
{"$param_expr": "-k / 2"} -sim_param("k") / 2, a parameter expression
{"$model": {...}} nested subsystem
{"$transition": {...}} sim_transition()

Files from a newer schema version are refused with a clear error rather than read incorrectly.

What can be saved

Everything that is declarative is portable:

  • all built-in blocks except fcn, ode and signal_function;
  • expression blocks, event resets given as strings, and state machine guards and actions given as strings;
  • subsystems and their instance parameters;
  • user block types registered with portable = TRUE.

Values must read back unchanged. Numeric, integer, logical and character vectors (with missing values and names), plain numeric matrices, lists of these and parameter references are saved exactly. Arrays with more than two dimensions, matrices with dimension names or of another type, factors, data frames and other classed values are refused when the model is written.

R functions cannot be represented safely. A model that contains them is refused, with the offending block named, instead of being saved without them:

bad <- sim_model("closure")
sim_add_block(bad, "constant", "u")
sim_add_block(bad, "fcn", "f", fun = function(u, t) u^2)
sim_connect(bad, "u", "f")
sim_write_json(bad, tempfile())
#> Error:
#> ! Block 'f' has type 'fcn', which is defined by R functions and cannot be written to a portable model file.

Replace such blocks with expression blocks where possible:

ok <- sim_model("portable")
sim_add_block(ok, "constant", "u", value = 3)
sim_add_block(ok, "expression", "f", expr = "u[1]^2")
sim_connect(ok, "u", "f")
sim_write_json(ok, f2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".json"))
sim_signal(sim_run(sim_compile(sim_read_json(f2)), c(0, 1), times = 1), "f")
#> f 
#> 9

Safety

Expression strings are parsed when the model is read and checked against a whitelist of arithmetic, comparison, logical and elementary functions. A file that tries to call anything else is rejected before anything runs:

txt <- readLines(f2)
txt <- sub("u\\[1\\]\\^2", "system('echo hi')", txt)
writeLines(txt, f3 <- tempfile(fileext = ".json"))
sim_read_json(f3)
#> Error:
#> ! Block 'f' (expression): `expr` uses functions that are not allowed in portable expressions: system.

Lists

sim_model_to_list() and sim_model_from_list() give the same representation as an R list, for storing models in other formats.
